Case_22003/figure2.png.source_caption: Figure 2: Chest X-ray demonstrating ground-glass opacities in the upper and lower lobes consistent with pneumonia.

description.short_caption: Chest X-ray showing bilateral ground-glass opacities in the upper and lower lobes.
description.detailed_description: This is an upright, frontal chest radiograph showing diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities predominantly in the upper and lower lobes. The heart size appears normal, and there is no evidence of pleural effusion. The lung markings are visible, and the opacities are patchy and ill-defined. The image includes monitoring leads visible on the chest.

Case_22003/figure1.png.source_caption: Figure 1: Respiratory panel obtained via nasopharyngeal swab

description.short_caption: Respiratory panel results from a nasopharyngeal swab.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a tabular report of a respiratory pathogen panel obtained via nasopharyngeal swab. The table lists various respiratory pathogens, including adenovirus, coronaviruses, influenza viruses, parainfluenza viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, and others. Each pathogen is marked as 'Not Detected' in the results column. The report includes a reference to the FDA website for further information about the test. The image is de-identified and includes a copyright notice from IDSA 2022.
visible_findings: Reference to FDA website for test information.

Case_22003/figure3.png.source_caption: Figure 3: Chest CT: Hazy ground glass densities in the lower lobes bilaterally with bilateral pleural effusions.

description.short_caption: Chest CT showing bilateral ground-glass opacities and pleural effusions.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image demonstrates bilateral hazy ground-glass opacities predominantly in the lower lobes. There are also bilateral pleural effusions visible, with fluid layering in the dependent portions of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinal structures appear central, and no significant shift is noted. The findings suggest a diffuse pulmonary process, possibly infectious or inflammatory in nature.
